comparisons.peer_summary: AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD focus on the integration of neural processing capabilities into AI PCs as a key driver for next-generation devices. While MU emphasizes the memory subsystem impact of these AI capabilities, AMD emphasizes the silicon-level integration strategy.

comparisons.peer_topic: Client CPU product launches and performance
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched Intel Core Ultra Series 1 (first with integrated NPU for AI workloads) and the power-efficient Intel Core Ultra 200V Series. Additionally, the 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors continued to serve a significant majority of client sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC identify the launch of AI-enabled client processors as a pivotal 2024 event reshaping the PC market. INTC details ramping sales of 'Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit' which 'introduced the first AI PCs to the market.' Similarly, MU describes 'next generation PCs that have been announced' containing 'high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI,' expecting these devices to have 'significantly more DRAM content.' Both disclosures link the specific hardware innovation (NPU/chipset) to the emerging 'AI PC' product category.

sentences.text: The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.

▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gamers and creators use NVIDIA GPUs for immersive experiences and content creation. The advent of generative AI is expected to drive broader adoption among PC users for local AI applications due to privacy, latency, and cost benefits.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA describe the expansion of AI workloads into the PC space as a significant market trend. MU states that as 'AI use cases proliferate to PCs, performance of the memory subsystem becomes more critical' and notes the announcement of low-power memory modules to support this. NVDA similarly observes that 'with the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC.' Both companies identify local PC AI execution as a growing driver, though they highlight different components (memory vs. GPU) as central to the experience.

sentences.text: As AI use cases proliferate to PCs, performance of the memory subsystem becomes more critical.

With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM discuss the role of specific neural processing hardware in enabling high-performance, low-power AI on devices. QCOM highlights its 'Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU' as a key processor for 'sustained, high-performance AI inference' within its AI Engine. MU similarly points to 'high-performance neural processing chipsets' in next-gen PCs as a feature driving higher DRAM demand. Both disclosures link the presence of dedicated AI silicon (NPU/chipset) to the capability of handling demanding AI workloads efficiently.

sentences.text: The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.

Our Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU is a key processor in our AI Engine and is designed for sustained, high-performance AI inference, enabling leading on-device AI capabilities with very low power consumption.
